text.p: HSBC James Capel said it had upgraded Brazilian private steelmaker Acesita to hold from sell.
-- said the company reported stronger and more consistent operational results in the first half of 1997, reflecting a trend reversal.
-- Acesita reported operating profit of $16.4 million in the first half, compared with a loss of $26.4 million in the same period a year ago.
-- "This improvement can be atributed to a significant reduction in production costs and we believe the results indicate a reversal trend," it said in a report.
-- HSBC James Capel noted, however, the company's high debt levels remain a concern.

-- It said Acesita's adjusted net earnings showed a loss of $18.3 million in the first half, compared with losses of $27.4 million in the same period last year. "This was caused by high net interest expenses of $51.3 million over the period. Lowering the company's debt in the future is the key to future performance," it said.
-- Acesita preferred was up 4.0 percent at 2.60 reais at 1125 local/1425 GMT on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
